title: Guru Nanak Rebukes Babur's Demand for Miracles

blocks.text: When Babur finally speaks, he asks why the Guru appears displeased with him and invites scrutiny of his own worth. He wants to know whether he is raw or ripe, true or false, as though spiritual authority were something that could be tested like a courtly riddle.
Guru Nanak refuses that frame. He explains that saints do not stage wonders for the vanity of kings and that no one should mistake spectacle for truth.
Instead, he directs Babur back toward the source of all real power. What men call miracle is only mercy or wrath from God, and neither can be manufactured to entertain ambition or flatter conquest.
